shared_turn_1.user_message: How does gum have calories if we don’t actually eat it?
shared_turn_1.assistant_response: Gum’s calories come from the parts that dissolve and get absorbed—sugar, sugar alcohols, flavorings—not the chewy base. When you chew, saliva breaks down the soluble ingredients, and you swallow them with saliva. Sugar-free gums often use xylitol/sorbitol, which have ~2 kcal/g and are partially absorbed/fermented. The gum base itself is mostly indigestible and passes through, so it contributes little/no usable energy. If you spit the gum out before swallowing, you avoid most of those calories; if you swallow it, you ingest the dissolved portion.
